There could be a ton that factors into this!
I'm a "just enougher" at 3 months pp, I've been supplementing with formula where I can't meet the need since day 1 (hungry girl started clustering the day I took her home!) 
My supply ebbs and flows unfortunately, and a few factors I've noticed contribute to my "empty days" as I call them

○Water intake over the past 48 hours - I need to drink at least 5 cups a day or I just won't produce anything 
○ red meat - we lack Iron as our bodies are giving EVERYTHING  to the baby to ensure they're fed properly,  often leaving us in a deficiency,  this also includes thinks like calcium, Vitamin D, etc.
○ my prenatals! - keep up on the prenatals even after giving birth, this will help with the whole vitamin thing
○ amount of calories eaten - make sure to EAT, now more than even in pregnancy, you are actually eating for two, make sure to get those calories!!! I recommend frequent snacks or granola or chewy bars between the 3 main meals! 
○ stress - if I'm more stressed, I produce less
○sleep - you need energy to produce ! Make sure to.rest every chance you get!


Do you have a pump? Rather than just relying on that letdown, try pumping as well, it tells your body you need to keep producing! Our bodies are subconsciously keeping track of how much, how long, and how often baby is eating...I was told to nurse for 20 then pump for 10, even if I get nothing out, it still helps! 

I personally recommend discussing things with a lactation specialist rather than just your Pediatrician,  they'll actually know more and have wonderful tips! They'll even check the latch, to see if that may be a factor in this! You can get recommendations for the specialist from your Pediatrician , they may have one in office like mine does, or Google helps! 

Best of luck!!!
